The lost girl took shelter in what seemed to be an empty house. Outside, through the window, she could see a motionless figure, and because it did not move she took it to be an inanimate object rather than a person. She was too unsettled to sleep and only finally slept from exhaustion. When she woke in the morning, the daylight let her see the figure's face—and she realized it was a real person whose face was turned toward her window, meaning it had been watching her all night while she slept. Realizing she had been observed the entire time by a stranger, and that the empty house offered no protection, she fled in terror.

The lost girl took shelter in an empty house and, through the window, saw a motionless figure outside. Because it never moved, she took it to be an inanimate object rather than a person, and this lurking presence kept her from sleeping until exhaustion finally overcame her. When she woke in the morning, the daylight let her see the truth: the figure was a real man standing at the window, whose face was turned toward her, and he had remained there motionless the whole night watching her sleep. Realizing that a stranger had been observing her all night while she was vulnerable, and that the empty house gave her no protection, she fled in terror.

The lost girl took shelter in an empty house and was too frightened to sleep. Through the window she saw a motionless figure outside; because it never moved, she took it for an inanimate object rather than a person. Exhaustion eventually made her sleep. In the morning, daylight showed her that the figure was in fact a real man standing at the window, his face turned toward her—he had been there all night watching her while she slept. Realizing that a stranger had observed her through the whole night while she was vulnerable and unprotected in the empty house, she fled in terror.
